title: Two-Pass Checkpointed Orbit Decomposition for the Hopalong Map: low-latency, Parallel, Low-Memory Implementation in Aether-Interpreter
topic: Hopalong Map – fast, parallel, low-memory – two-pass checkpointed orbit decomposition
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: The Hopalong map is a chaotic dynamical system whose orbit generation is traditionally memory-intensive and sequential. We present a two-pass algorithm that records checkpoints at regular intervals, enabling parallel reconstruction of the full orbit with only $O(1)$ additional memory per thread. The method preserves the strict height-balanced invariant of an implicit balanced search structure while guaranteeing that each segment recomputation remains $O(\log N)$. We prove that the overall asymptotic complexity is $O(N \log N)$ for $N$ orbit steps, and that the checkpointing overhead is bounded by a constant factor independent of $N$. The implementation is written in pure Aether-Interpreter and demonstrates that checkpointed reconstruction scales linearly with the number of processing cores on a single-socket AMD EPYC 7763 system. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Aether-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261101_210119_hopalong_map__fast__parallel}
